items.description: Kitchen leak detection, moisture measurement and call-out
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.7(e)–(g) cover locating the concealed leak, measuring affected areas, necessary labour and one call-out; the combined billing is permitted under 7.1.8(e). Using Case 21 as a benchmark, about €650 for 14 technician-hours plus €840 for call-out, acoustic pinpointing and moisture measurement gives €1,490 gross, without a second travel charge.

items.description: Expose, repair and re-insulate kitchen supply pipe
items.rationale: Sections 2.4.3(a) and 7.1.7(a), (c) and (g) support local access and like-for-like repair of the failed indoor pipe. Allow about €140 for access, €195 for replacing the documented 1.5 m copper run with like-for-like fittings, and €65 for stripping and replacing the foam lagging, for €400 gross.

Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge on each contractor's invoice. This is the plumber's only travel charge and is separate from the leak detection firm's call-out; allow €76 gross, consistent with Case 21.

items.description: Dry affected kitchen floor and wall base
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) and (e) cover drying the measured wet floor and wall base, equipment hire and completion readings. Allow about €60 for one condensation dryer for nearly seven days and €130 for setup, collection and final checks, for €190 gross with no separate electricity allowance under 7.1.8(d).
